data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense fails because redefining rational action as 'strategic selection of the most falsifiable survivor' to maximize error elimination implicitly assumes that past severity is a reliable indicator of future testability. This assumption—that a theory which survived severe tests yesterday will continue to be the most efficient vehicle for finding errors tomorrow—is itself an inductive leap about the stability of the testing environment, which Popper explicitly rejected. Without this inductive bridge, there is no non-arbitrary reason to prefer the better-corroborated theory over a new, equally bold conjecture that has not yet been tested.
